A Welcome From
our headmaster
“At Thorngrove School, we are proud to offer a warm, nurturing, and family-oriented environment where children aged 2½ to 13 can thrive. From the very start of their journey in our exceptional Nursery, each child is supported and inspired to reach their full potential.
Our architect-designed buildings are set within 25 acres of beautiful grounds, providing the perfect setting for learning, exploration, and growth. We are committed to delivering an outstanding education, exceptional pastoral care, and a truly enriching experience for every child who becomes part of the Thorngrove community.”

SEE FOR YOURSELF
BOOK A TOUR
Discover the charm of Thorngrove School, where education meets nature in a stunning countryside setting. Our beautiful grounds, rich with greenery and wildlife, provide the perfect environment for curiosity, creativity, and growth. Come and experience the warmth of our community, explore our exceptional facilities, and see firsthand how we inspire young minds.
our AIMS
Be Curious
Curiosity is at the heart of learning. We provide consistently excellent and exciting teaching which enables every pupil to develop intellectual enquiry. Our aim is to ignite and nurture a lifelong love of learning. These efforts build upon our unchanged founding pillars: Inspiration, Confidence, and Achievement
Be Community-Minded
Encouraging sensitivity and empathy is key to our approach. We help pupils develop these qualities towards those around them and in the wider world. Additionally, we actively promote well-being, mindfulness, and a strong sense of worth in all our pupils.
Be Challenged
At Thorngrove, we are dedicated to helping every child achieve their full potential. This means maximising academic results in all internal, standardised, and external examinations. Beyond academics, we focus on building resilience and promoting a positive mind-set among all our pupils.
Be Creative
We believe in enabling pupils, regardless of their ability, to discover and develop their individual talents. This includes a wide range of activities such as Sport, the Performing and Creative Arts, and other enriching pursuits. Our goal is to provide opportunities for every child to shine.
“A wide range of extra-curricular activities provide pupils with enjoyable and meaningful learning experiences. This is a significant strength of the school. Pupils across the school thrive during weekly lessons in the woods, which support their physical, mental and emotional wellbeing through effective teaching.”
“Staff in early years use cleverly crafted questions and modelling to encourage the development of children’s language.”
“Pupils across the school are articulate. They express their ideas and discuss their learning confidently. The calm and purposeful atmosphere around the school is strengthened by pupils’ respectful relationships between staff and each other.”
“Pupils acquire new knowledge and understanding because of effective teaching.”

Before the holidays, Mrs McSorland had the absolute pleasure of taking her Reception class on an unforgettable tour of cruise ship, Liberty of the Seas! All of the planning and risk assessments were certainly worth it because, as Elliott put it, it was "the BEST trip EVER!" The children explored every possible nook and cranny, including areas that are usually off-limits to guests. Highlights included the incredible ice rink, chatting with the officers on the bridge, and discovering just how tiny the ship's steering wheel really is! After walking over 10,000 steps before lunch, some well-earned downtime in the kids' club was just what everyone needed. Lunch in the Windjammer buffet was another exciting part of the day, especially being served strawberry and kiwi juice while waiting to choose from the fantastic selection of food. Unsurprisingly, multiple desserts quickly disappeared! A huge thank you to everyone who gave up their time to support the trip, and a very special thank you to @royalcaribbean and Hudson's dad, for such an incredible opportunity. It was a memorable day of exploration, learning and fun – an experience the children will be talking about for a long time. #thorngroveschool #prepschool #prepschoollife #receptionclass #pickyourpath

All pupils from Nursery to Year 8 took part, completing the various obstacles around the school grounds. Wrap-around care & Holiday Clubs
What's in this section?
At Thorngrove we understand that some parents need ‘wrap-around’ care to allow for their busy working lifestyle.
We run a Breakfast Club Monday to Thursday from 7.30am. Pupils can be dropped off at the New Hall where they are looked after by a member of staff and offered a selection of toast, cereals, fruit and eggs for breakfast.
In the afternoon, we run an aftercare facility which is available every day after school. It is located in the Old Hall and supervised by member of Thorngrove staff. The children will be given a snack to keep them going. They have many toys, games and activities available to them. The Aftercare facility starts at 3.15pm in the afternoon and finishes at 5.30pm. For more information about the cost of Breakfast Club and Aftercare, please ask the school office.
Holiday Club is also very popular, and we have teamed up with SuperCamps to enable us to offer clubs during every half-term and holiday. SuperCamps create fun and interesting activities to keep the children entertained, even on wet days! For more information please visit the SuperCamps website (link below) or pop into the school office.

Sports Curriculum
What's in this section?
At Thorngrove, we believe Games and PE are important for developing mental well-being as well as physical fitness, team work, resilience and social skills.
Sport is an integral part of the education we offer. Our ‘sports for all’ philosophy ensures that every child enjoys regular exercise and the experience of learning new sports.
All pupils from nursery to year 8 have regular PE and games lessons with specialist teachers. For pupils in years 3 to 8 weekly matches against a range of local prep schools take place on Wednesday and Friday afternoons. A wide variety of lunchtime and after-school sports clubs also take place, including (but not limited to) football, rugby, netball, hockey, cross-country, ballet, cricket, tennis, and judo.
Our sporting curriculum is designed to foster physical awareness, mental wellbeing, team spirit, an understanding of getting out of life what you put in, as well as learning to lose and win with good grace. Frequently on the athletics track the loudest cheers are for those who are coming in last or who pick themselves up from a fall and carry on!
Thorngrove has an enviable record of sporting achievements at local and regional level, but whether your child is naturally sporty or not, they will be taught by specialist teachers from an early age and will be included in regular house and inter-school matches. They will be encouraged to enjoy sport and maintain an active lifestyle during their time at Thorngrove and beyond. The Sports Department also takes regular tours in the UK and abroad – most recently a football and hockey tour to Valencia.

Performing Arts
What's in this section?
Thorngrove is renowned for its Performing Arts programme. Children are exposed to drama, dance and music at an early age and enjoy performing in front of their peers and parents on a regular basis.
Music is at the heart of the school and Thorngrove takes immense pride in its outstanding musical achievements, showcasing the talent and dedication of our pupils. Over the years, our music program has nurtured a vast range of musical abilities, from gifted solo performers to harmonious ensembles.
Not only do pupils shine in the traditional domains of classical music, but they also embrace contemporary genres, demonstrating versatility and creativity. Our music faculty, coupled with a supportive learning environment and a wonderful team of peripatetic teachers, has propelled our students to reach remarkable heights, embodying true musical excellence.
Drama and the performing arts are a hugely popular part of school life. Children are exposed to drama at an early age and perform in front of their peers and parents on a regular basis. Drama is taught as part of the English curriculum and from Year 3 as a separate subject by a specialist drama teacher.
Every child has the opportunity to be in productions whilst at Thorngrove. These have included The Little Mermaid, Matilda, Shrek and The Lion King.
Throughout the year, trips are arranged to local theatres, including the Watermill (with whom we are a partner school) and national theatres, including The Globe and theatres in the West End.
LAMDA Speech and Drama lessons are extremely popular with exams being held on the school site each term. We are proud that our pupils have enjoyed remarkable success in this field.

ISI Inspection Reports
What's in this section?
Rare "Significant strength" awarded
Thorngrove School was inspected by the Independent Schools Inspectorate (ISI) on behalf of the Department for Education from 11th-13th June 2024.
This inspection was part of the new Framework for inspections introduced in September 2023 which has moved away from graded judgements. ‘Framework 23’ places an emphasis on pupil voice and wellbeing and allows the inspectors to spend extended time with pupils and gain a deeper understanding of the schools they visit.
Thorngrove was found to have met the standard in all areas which is the highest grade possible under ‘Framework 23’.
The standards focused on are:
The inspecting team were quickly able to recognise the positive influence that Thorngrove has on the pupils’ development across the board. Extra-curricular provision comes in for particular praise, being identified as a ‘significant strength’ of the school. “The wide range of extra-curricular activities that provide the pupils with enjoyable and meaningful experiences.” The ISI rarely denotes a ‘significant strength’ in its reports, and the bar is set extremely high – any such provision must result in a clear, demonstrable and highly-beneficial impact for pupils. We are incredibly proud to receive this exceptional accolade, currently only awarded to 16% of inspected Prep Schools in the country.
Below are a few extracts from the report. The full report can be downloaded at the link below or a printed copy of the report is available on request from the School Office.

Enrichment and Clubs
What's in this section?
Introduced in 2022 the Thorngrove ‘Be’ Programme is designed to provide pupils with a broader range of experiences and help to develop their character, providing them with opportunities to further harness skills that will allow them to flourish in 21st Century life.
The programme focusses on four key strands which align with the Aims of the school:
Pupils spend the afternoon every Tuesday undertaking activities within one of these areas.
The world is a large and diverse place, and we think it is important that pupils are exposed to this in a productive and thought-provoking way.
As a school we are also committed to developing the character of the pupils within the school. Greater exposure to a wider range of opportunities will help them develop core skills such as collaboration, perseverance, problem solving and communication, all of which enable them to develop as well-rounded individuals.
A variety of clubs are also available to pupils throughout the year. The activities vary widely and children can choose to be in as many or as few as they want. They take place at lunch break and after school and the full list of clubs is published at the start of each term.
Most activities are free to do apart from ballet, judo and street dance.
A current list of activities is available from the school office.

The Creative Arts
What's in this section?
ART
Art is an important part of life at Thorngrove. We provide a rich and varied curriculum which fosters curiosity, resourcefulness and creativity, alongside the acquisition of technical skills in drawing, painting, sculpture and printing.
In weekly Art lessons, children learn to select, use and manipulate materials and media for particular effects, making creative choices for their own work. They investigate artworks and explore styles, approaches and techniques used in contemporary and traditional practice, celebrating the diversity of Art and developing visual literacy.
Many additional opportunities in Art are offered through our extracurricular programmes and scholarship groups. Pottery, Photography and Textiles are amongst the courses included in a wide selection of Art clubs and Enrichment projects. At Thorngrove, we aim to nurture a lifelong love of Art and give children the experiences needed to successfully express their creative ideas and become confident artists of the future.
D&T
D&T is taught in a spacious and well-equipped workshop. Pupils are able to discover the different stages of a design process and the various tools, materials and techniques required to turn their dreams and ideas into reality.
There is hardly anything more fulfilling for a pupil than to produce a quality item with their own imagination and their own hands: a rewarding tangible three-dimensional proof of their ability. Tools are introduced carefully, and every student has a chance to practise before embarking on their main projects. Confidence in tool handling is built up progressively and more tools, machines and materials become available to the pupils throughout their time here. We focus on a huge variety of project work incorporating traditional techniques and modern technology such as the laser cutter to cut, etch and engrave.
Thorngrove is continually investing in Design and Technology as we believe it is a vital part of the creative programme.

Pastoral Care
What's in this section?
At Thorngrove, we pride ourselves on our outstanding pastoral care. Family is at the heart of our ethos, and we like to think of the school as an extension of each child’s family.
When a child joins Thorngrove, their form teacher is their first point of pastoral contact. The form teacher plays a vital role in helping children settle into their new environment—supporting them in building friendships, becoming familiar with daily routines and feeling secure both inside and outside the classroom. With small classes across the school, teachers get to know the children well, understanding what makes them tick, their interests and their ambitions. Form teachers are also the first port of call for parents with any queries.
In addition to the form teacher, each pupil is supported by a Head of Section, who has overarching responsibility for their pastoral and academic welfare during their time in that part of the school. Heads of Section work closely with form teachers on a daily basis to ensure that all pupils are happy, confident, and thriving.
Our Heads of Section are:
Beyond this, we have a dedicated and experienced wellbeing team that includes a qualified School Counsellor, two trained Emotional Literacy Support Assistants (ELSAs), and a number of paediatric first aid-trained staff across the school—including in the office and our teaching assistant team. Children have access to both emotional and physical care throughout the school day. Our Medical Room supports children with any bumps or bruises they may sustain, while The Snug offers a calm, quiet space for those who may be feeling overwhelmed or need time to regulate their emotions.
Our Year 8 pupils, guided by the staff, also take on leadership roles as ‘buddies’ to the younger children. They help during morning registration, they play together at break times, and provide ongoing support throughout the week. This fosters a culture of care and responsibility and sets a positive example for the whole school community. Pupil voice is highly valued at Thorngrove. Our active School Council includes representatives from every year group (Reception to Year 8) and provides a forum for meaningful discussion, inclusion, and change. The Council plays an important role in shaping school life, with many initiatives and ideas coming directly from the children themselves.
Another important layer of pastoral support comes from our Heads of House. Every child at Thorngrove belongs to one of four Houses - Ash, Beech, Oak or Rowan - and remains in their House throughout their time at the school. These Houses nurture a sense of family, teamwork, healthy competition, and friendship. House meetings take place regularly each term and contribute significantly to the school’s supportive, community spirit.
Pastoral care at Thorngrove is overseen by our Senior Deputy Head (Pastoral), Mr Tom Layton, who meets regularly with staff to discuss any concerns and ensure that each child’s needs are fully understood and supported. These regular meetings help us maintain a well-rounded, consistent picture of the children in our care. At Thorngrove, we are proud to be a warm, welcoming, and close-knit school community. We believe that feeling safe, known, and valued is the foundation for every child to flourish.

Directors
What's in this section?
Thorngrove School was founded in 1988 by Nick and Connie Broughton. After several years of teaching in London, they chose to move to the beautiful Hampshire countryside to start their family and establish a school rooted in warmth, ambition, and community.
Thanks to its success and unique atmosphere, Thorngrove flourished and grew year on year. There are currently over 200 pupils at the school.
In the summer of 2009, Nick and Connie stepped back from the day-to-day running of the school to take up their roles as Directors, appointing their Deputy Head, Adam King, as Headmaster. In September 2022, Adam was succeeded by Nick Graham, who assumed the role following five years as Senior Deputy Head. The Broughtons remain very much part of daily life at Thorngrove. They are often seen walking their dogs, Raffy and Rory, around the grounds and continue to take a genuine interest in the happiness and well-being of every child.
In September 2022, the Broughtons appointed a Board of Directors consisting of eight members (see list below).
Nick Broughton - Director and Chair of the Board
Nick founded Thorngrove School with his wife, Connie, in 1988 on their family farm, with the vision of creating a nurturing and family-focused education for their four children.
He studied Mathematics at the University of East Anglia and began his career as a lecturer at Newbury College of Further Education, later teaching in London where he met Connie. The couple then moved to Barcelona to teach English as a foreign language before returning to Newbury, where Nick taught at Barton Peveril Sixth Form College.
After five years running the family farm, Nick combined his passion for education and community to establish Thorngrove, which has since grown into the thriving school it is today.
Connie Broughton - Director and Secretary
Connie co-founded Thorngrove with her husband, Nick, in 1988, and together they led the school until 2009. Alongside her leadership role, she was a dedicated form teacher and taught Latin to the older pupils. Connie studied Spanish and French at London University and went on to teach both subjects in senior schools before moving to Highclere, where the idea of founding a school first took shape.
In 2023, she published a book about the founding of Thorngrove entitled ‘An Interesting Experiment’, with proceeds supporting the Brain Tumour Charity. Connie takes great pride in the fact that all four of her children – and now ten grandchildren – have attended, or are currently attending, Thorngrove.
James Broughton - Director
James graduated from Goldsmiths College, London with a BA Ed Hons degree and began his career teaching Design and Technology at an SEN school in London. He later returned to Newbury, the area where he grew up, and is now proud to have two sons at Thorngrove.
Passionate about hands-on learning, James helped introduce both beekeeping and pig husbandry to the school. He also enjoys putting his DIY skills to use behind the scenes, building sets for Thorngrove’s ambitious school productions.
Jessica Thomas - Director responsible for Health and Safety
Jessica graduated from the University of Bristol with a BA Hons in Classics, before completing an MA in Ceramics. She began her career in publishing, working for several years as an editor at Penguin Random House, before relocating to the countryside to raise her three children.
In 2016, she retrained as a teacher and is now Thorngrove’s Head of Latin. In addition to leading the department, she contributes to the school’s broader cultural life through the creative and performing arts enrichment programmes.
Jessica also serves as Director with responsibility for Health and Safety, ensuring the highest standards of care and compliance across the school.
Bryony Wingfield Digby - Director responsible for Safeguarding
Bryony studied Sculpture at the University of Leeds before completing her PGCE in Art and Design at the University of Brighton. She later gained a CELTA qualification and spent two exciting years teaching English as a Foreign Language in Buenos Aires. A practising artist, she has taught at Marlborough College and now at St Edward’s, where she continues to share her love of creativity with young people.
As a former Thorngrove pupil herself, Bryony is delighted to have come full circle and return as Director. With all three of her children now happily at Thorngrove, she feels especially proud to be part of the school community once again.
Miranda Price - Director
Miranda graduated from Cardiff University with a BA (Hons) in Ancient History before completing a PGCE specialising in Early Years. She spent many years as a Nursery Teacher at a Prep School in Dulwich before joining Thorngrove in 2012 to lead the Nursery.
Now an integral member of the Pre-Prep team, Miranda is often the first point of contact for new Thorngrove families. She is a firm believer in the school’s ethos and values, which she promotes while caring for the youngest children. With both of her children attending Thorngrove, Miranda is a passionate and active member of the whole school community.
Charlotte Fraser - Non-Executive Director
Charlotte Fraser is a Thorngrove parent and has been a director since 2022. Charlotte read Modern Languages at Brasenose College, Oxford. She then trained as a lawyer and is a Partner at Farrer & Co, where she runs the firm's Contentious Trusts and Estates team.
Gareth Jones - Non-Executive Director
With an English with History degree and a Masters in Educational Leadership, Gareth is an experienced and passionate educationalist who has worked in the prep sector for over 25 years. He started his career at the Dragon School in Oxford where, among many things, he was Director of Sport, Director of the Extended Curriculum, a Housemaster and Chair of the Common Room. From there he spent six years as Head of St Andrew’s Prep in Eastbourne before moving, in 2021, to Bilton Grange in Warwickshire, as Headmaster. Bilton Grange is part of the Rugby School Group and Gareth’s role includes being part of the Executive Leadership Team for the Group which now has several schools in the UK as well as a growing number overseas.
An active member of IAPS, the organisation that supports prep schools, Gareth has sat on both the sports and pastoral committees and is co-chair of one of their school networks. He was a governor of a state infant school before joining Thorngrove in a non-executive Director role, in September 2022.

Nursery
What's in this section?
Thorngrove Nursery – where confidence and creativity shine!
At Thorngrove, we welcome children from the age of two and a half into a nurturing and inspiring environment. Set within two vibrant, cosy, and happy rooms, our youngest children settle quickly, feeling right at home - allowing their confidence, curiosity, and creativity to flourish.
Our Nursery is situated within the main school building, complete with a dedicated outdoor space and a direct link to the Reception classroom. This thoughtful layout supports high levels of attainment and ensures a smooth, natural transition into the next stage of their learning journey.
Children benefit from the full range of Thorngrove’s beautiful facilities, regularly enjoying the woodlands, school grounds, and eco spaces. They also have access to specialist teaching in French, P.E., Ballet, Music, and Forest School - enriching their experiences and broadening their horizons from an early age.
We are especially proud of the way our environment, teaching, and carefully planned activities positively shape our children. Their happiness, confidence, and grounded outlook are immediately apparent to all who visit.
Thorngrove Nursery is a truly special place—where children are free to be themselves, and their unique spark is recognised, nurtured, and encouraged to shine.

Academic Life
What's in this section?
At Thorngrove School, academic life is considered one of the most important areas, with a commitment to providing an education that enables all children to develop their full intellectual, physical, aesthetic, creative, emotional, spiritual, and social potential. The school aims to foster skilled, independent learners with an intellectual curiosity that will equip them for future life. Pupils are encouraged to engage in the 'Learning Pit', a concept where they undertake challenging tasks to deepen their understanding of topic work, build their resilience and encourage them to be critical and collaborative thinkers.
Thorngrove School believes in inspiring children to love learning through an atmosphere of fun, exploration, and discovery in lessons led by well-qualified and experienced teachers. The curriculum is clearly structured to enable children to achieve within a stimulating, challenging, and supportive learning environment, promoting enthusiasm and enjoyment.
The school's curriculum follows the National Curriculum Framework alongside the requirements of ISEB. Thorngrove prepares children for senior school entrance exams, scholarships, and Common Entrance assessment. It offers a broad curriculum that prioritises a strong academic core of subjects, while also developing pupils' independent learning skills and resilience through motivating and supportive teaching.
Reading is central to the English Department's approach. The curriculum is built around high-quality texts, offering opportunities to explore important themes, different cultural settings, traditional and contemporary literature, language use, discussion, and reflection.
Each book acts as a "springboard" for developing essential speaking, listening, and comprehension skills, writing for various audiences and purposes, and improving spelling, punctuation, and grammar.
The school aims to develop a lifelong love of reading, fostering it through quality texts, enthusiastic teaching, competitions, a school reading dog, and special celebration days. It is believed that the more "technical" aspects of English come more easily when children enjoy lessons and are "hooked by a book".
Maths is seen as an integral part of life, with the aim for children to develop a solid foundation and the confidence to navigate their future journey. Pupils are encouraged to think through problems, review evidence, and arrive at conclusions, fostering confidence to learn from mistakes and build resilience.
The department promotes a positive relationship with maths, developing imagination and flexible thought.
Children are taught to work both independently and collaboratively, understanding how maths connects across subjects and its importance in life. Key skills and concepts are revisited and built upon year by year to deepen understanding.
A sound knowledge of Science is considered essential for all children to understand life in the 21st Century. Science encourages critical thinking, developing a "how and why" approach to look beyond basic facts, question assumptions, and identify patterns and consequences in data.
Understanding Science helps children appreciate and relate to the rapidly changing world. It teaches them to make observations, collect information, and draw conclusions by being reflective and observing closely. Mistakes are valued as learning opportunities in a safe environment.
The Science curriculum aims to capture students' curiosity through a wide range of exciting and challenging experiments and investigations. Practical teaching is emphasised as crucial for making Science accessible and enjoyable. Pupils are encouraged to take their love of Science out of the lab and into the real world.
Language learning is highly regarded. Children learn French from nursery up to the end of Year 8. While French is the primary language taught, Spanish and German can be offered as extra-curricular activities.
In Year 7, children participate in a week of "total immersion" in Normandy, France, staying at a purpose-built chateau. They are encouraged to speak French constantly and experience authentic French culture through activities like fencing, excursions to local markets, and a chocolate factory. This experience is valuable preparation for the listening and speaking parts of the French Common Entrance (CE) exams.

Charity and Community Links
What's in this section?
At Thorngrove we believe in supporting and helping local and national charities and forging links with the community.
Each year the pupils vote from a short list, chosen by the School Council, for the charity they would like to support for that school year. Over recent years, we have supported Swings & Smiles, Medical Detection Dogs and The Brain Tumour Charity.
Over the years, Thorngrove (along with the Friends of Thorngrove) held numerous events to help raise much-needed funds for their chosen charity. Examples of these include -
In addition to the charity partnerships, we love working with the local community.
Each year we open the School to Woolton Hill Surgery for their annual winter flu vaccinations. The Woolton Hill Village Market has relocated to our Hall for their outstanding market which takes place every 4 to 6 weeks, selling local produce to over 900 visitors. We also support West Berkshire Foodbank and collect donations from our parents throughout the year.

Welcome to
Pre-Prep
welcome to pre-prep from
our Head of Lower School
"My two daughters and I began our Thorngrove adventure together in 2013, and just two years later, I had the privilege of becoming Head of Pre-Prep—known to us as the Lower School. If anyone asks, I will always say I have the best job in the school!
In Lower School, we are a team of like-minded, passionate educators dedicated to making each child’s experience truly exceptional. We wholeheartedly believe that children learn best in a kind, calm, and supportive environment - where resilience is second nature and there’s no such thing as failure, only opportunities to learn and grow.
Walk into any classroom, and you’ll find smiles, laughter, and a genuine sense of belonging. Here, everyone is known, valued, and cared for. The sense of family is real and deeply felt - it’s far more than just a hashtag.
Our purpose-built classrooms open directly onto age-appropriate outdoor learning spaces, and yes - waterproof boiler suits are a must! We head outside in all weathers because learning at Thorngrove doesn’t stop at the classroom door.
Children in the Lower School benefit from an enriched curriculum delivered by specialist teachers in Forest School, Music, Drama, ICT, Ballet, French, and PE - all using the same high-quality resources as our older pupils. Daily sessions in Anima Phonics and mathematics help build strong foundations, while themed topic days bring learning to life in the most engaging and memorable ways.
Thorngrove Lower School — Simply the best!"

BOOK A TOUR
Come and visit us in Lower School and see first-hand how we help every child to reach for the stars by planting strong roots from the very start.
our AIMS
Be Curious
Curiosity is at the heart of learning. We provide consistently excellent and exciting teaching which enables every pupil to develop intellectual enquiry. Our aim is to ignite and nurture a lifelong love of learning. These efforts build upon our unchanged founding pillars: Inspiration, Confidence, and Achievement
Be Community-Minded
Encouraging sensitivity and empathy is key to our approach. We help pupils develop these qualities towards those around them and in the wider world. Additionally, we actively promote well-being, mindfulness, and a strong sense of worth in all our pupils.
Be Challenged
At Thorngrove, we are dedicated to helping every child achieve their full potential. This means maximising academic results in all internal, standardised, and external examinations. Beyond academics, we focus on building resilience and promoting a positive mind-set among all our pupils.
Be Creative
We believe in enabling pupils, regardless of their ability, to discover and develop their individual talents. This includes a wide range of activities such as Sport, the Performing and Creative Arts, and other enriching pursuits. Our goal is to provide opportunities for every child to shine.
“A wide range of extra-curricular activities provide pupils with enjoyable and meaningful learning experiences. This is a significant strength of the school. Pupils across the school thrive during weekly lessons in the woods, which support their physical, mental and emotional wellbeing through effective teaching.”
“Staff in early years use cleverly crafted questions and modelling to encourage the development of children’s language.”
“Pupils across the school are articulate. They express their ideas and discuss their learning confidently. The calm and purposeful atmosphere around the school is strengthened by pupils’ respectful relationships between staff and each other.”
“Pupils acquire new knowledge and understanding because of effective teaching.”
